title: `labelled_spss` metadata are not retained when saving SPSS files
description:
When saving a tibble with `labelled_spss` variables (as opposed to just `labelled` variables) to an SPSS file, none of the metadata from the `labelled_spss` variables are actually saved.

Note that `labelled_spss` variables are automatically created when importing (`read_spss()`) SPSS files using the `user_na = TRUE` argument, so this bug makes round-tripping SPSS files not possible.

Here’s an reprex:

```r
library(tibble)
library(haven)
 
# Create example data
x = c(1,2,1,9)
d = tibble(
  x1 = labelled(x, labels = c(no = 1, yes = 2, unknown = 9)),
  x2 = labelled_spss(x, labels = c(no = 1, yes = 2, unknown = 9), na_values = 9)
)
 
# Look at the data (all metadata are correctly stored)
str(d$x1)
#> Class 'labelled'  atomic [1:4] 1 2 1 9
#>   ..- attr(*, "labels")= Named num [1:3] 1 2 9
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "no" "yes" "unknown"
str(d$x2)
#> Classes 'labelled_spss', 'labelled'  atomic [1:4] 1 2 1 9
#>   ..- attr(*, "labels")= Named num [1:3] 1 2 9
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "no" "yes" "unknown"
#>   ..- attr(*, "na_values")= num 9

# Save the data
write_sav(d, "labs.sav")
 
# Read the data (in two different ways)
d2 = read_spss("labs.sav")
d3 = read_spss("labs.sav", user_na = TRUE)
 
# The x1 variables are OK
str(d2$x1)
#> Class 'labelled'  atomic [1:4] 1 2 1 9
#>   ..- attr(*, "format.spss")= chr "F8.2"
#>   ..- attr(*, "labels")= Named num [1:3] 1 2 9
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "no" "yes" "unknown"
str(d3$x1)
#> Class 'labelled'  atomic [1:4] 1 2 1 9
#>   ..- attr(*, "format.spss")= chr "F8.2"
#>   ..- attr(*, "labels")= Named num [1:3] 1 2 9
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "no" "yes" "unknown"

# But the x2 variables are now missing ~all their metadata
str(d2$x2)
#>  atomic [1:4] 1 2 1 9
#>  - attr(*, "format.spss")= chr "F8.2"
str(d3$x2)
#>  atomic [1:4] 1 2 1 9
#>  - attr(*, "format.spss")= chr "F8.2"
```

The reprex shows that the `x1` data (`labelled`) are correctly saved and read, while the `x2` data (`labelled_spss`) are not correctly saved. (The bug is in *saving* the SPSS file, not in reading the file. If I open the saved filed in SPSS, the metadata is missing. And if I manually add the metadata in SPSS and then save the file, the metadata *is* correctly imported in R with `read_spss()`.)

I have tested above code using the latest Git version of the `haven` package (*and* the latest CRAN version).

title: labelled sensitive to labels ordering in Stata
description:
When defining a labelled object, the label-value vector needs to be sorted by its numerical values, or else Stata cannot correctly read the label:

``` r
library(haven)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

labs <- c(Democrat = 1, Republican = 2, Independent = 3) # named vector

lbl <- tibble(pid3 = labelled(1L:3L, labs)) # both sorted
lbl_num <- tibble(pid3 = labelled(3L:1L, labs)) # values not sorted
lbl_lab <- tibble(pid3 = labelled(3L:1L, labs[c(1, 3, 2)])) # labels not sorted

write_dta(lbl, "foo.dta")
write_dta(lbl_num, "foo_num.dta")
write_dta(lbl_lab, "foo_lab.dta") # this one gets misread in Stata
```

When I open `foo_lab.dta` in Stata, I get
```

. tab pid3

       pid3 |      Freq.     Percent        Cum.
------------+-----------------------------------
   Democrat |          1       33.33       33.33
          2 |          1       33.33       66.67
Independent |          1       33.33      100.00
------------+-----------------------------------
      Total |          3      100.00
```
So the label for `2` dropped out. Is this a bug?

This error does not occur when the dta file is read into R by `read_dta` and analyze it there; only when I open it in Stata.

title: parso Java library (not an issue)
description:
In case it's helpful...

Matt Shotwell has a package on github called sas7bdat.parso. It's a wrapper for the GGA Software Parso Java library (ask Google).

I've used Parso to read many dozens of .sas7bdat files without problems (well, the only problem I've found is unescaped quotes in their csv writer - but that's the csv writer, not the sas7bdat reader). I know someone who is working on having Parso turn a bunch of SAS datasets directly into a SQLite db to avoid the whole csv nonsense.

For info, Parso was written because they couldn't get Sassy Reader to do what they wanted. Sassy Reader was based on Matt Shotwells package.

Again, I hope it helps.
Harry

title: read_spss() doesn’t handle non-ASCII characters in variable names properly
description:
I have an example SPSS file with a few non-ASCII characters. When I import this using read_spss(), the non-ASCII characters in variable values are handled properly, but the same characters in variable **names** are not converted. They look like what UTF-8 byte sequences look when interpreted as ISO-8859-1 byte sequences do. If you supply an e-mail address, I can mail you the example file (the GitHub issue tracker doesn’t seem to support attachments).

[1] "unknown" "unknown" "unknown"

title: Haven API updates
description:
From @evanmiller

Quick API update you should be aware of. The "error_handler" now receives a second argument: the user_ctx variable that is passed to all the other callbacks.

I've also added another callback for progress indicators, may or may not be useful to you:

``` c
typedef int (*readstat_progress_handler)(double progress, void *ctx);

readstat_error_t readstat_set_progress_handler(
    readstat_parser_t *parser,
    readstat_progress_handler progress_handler);
```

This callback periodically receives a double between 0.0 and 1.0 indicating the % progress through reading a file. I implemented it mainly so I could get a progress indicator on POR files, since as we've discussed the row count is not available in advance. But the progress handler should work on all file types.

title: write_spss() value labels where 0 is a possible value
description:
I find that when writing an SPSS file with a variable that contains 0 as a level, in the resulting .sav that variable will be shifted so that the label and value for 0 is now 1, and so on.

For example

``` r test, eval=FALSE
dummy <- data.frame(gen = c(0,1,1,0,1,0,1,1))

dummy$gen <- factor(dummy$gen, levels=c(0,1), labels=c('Female', 'Male'))

haven::write_sav(dummy, 'genderDummy.sav')
```

In the resulting .sav, "Female" takes the value of 1 and "Male" takes the value of 2, which is different than what is desired. 

There are other cases in which I need the value of 0 to have a value label. 

I'm not sure if this is a bug or if there is a workaround I am not aware of. Thanks for the help.

title: missing values treatment
description:
The following public file might help explaining the issue:
http://www.columbia.edu/itc/hs/pubhealth/remler/8502/client_edit/datasets/gss.ZIP

``` R
> library(haven)
> aa <- read_spss("gss.sav")
> table(aa$DEGREE)
  0   1   2   3   4 
279 780  90 234 113
> attr(aa$DEGREE, "labels")
  Less than HS    High school Junior college       Bachelor       Graduate 
             0              1              2              3              4 
Not applicable     Don't know      No answer 
             7              8              9 
> library(foreign)
> bb <- read.spss("gss.sav", use.value.labels=FALSE, to.data.frame=TRUE, use.missings=FALSE)
>  table(bb$DEGREE)
  0   1   2   3   4   8   9 
279 780  90 234 113   2   2
```

As you can see, haven has automatically recoded all the missing values to NAs, whereas read.spss() allows the user decide what to do with those values. It is important, for example in missing values imputation, to know which NAs are due to "Don't know" and which are due to "No answer".

Would it be possible to have haven's read_spss() function (and generally any function in haven that imports labelled variables) to allow users decide what to do with the missing values?

Adrian

title: Importing dates and datetime with read_dta
description:
I just updated haven to the last version and I have prepared a Stata file available at http://joseph.larmarange.net/stata_dates.dta
- Variable _date_ has `%td` format and is imported correctly.
- _datetime_ has `%tc` format and is imported correctly
- _date2_ has `%tdCCYY-NN-DD` format, which means it's a date with custom display format. It's not imported as a date.  In fact, any format starting with `%td`, regardless of the following character should be imported as a date  (same thing with other Stata formats)
- _datetime2_ has `%tC` format and seems to be imported correctly
- _year_ has `%ty` format (year format). It's imported correctly as an atomic vector, containing the year
- _months_, _week_, _quarter_ and _halfyear_ are specific format from Stata, respectively `%tm`, `%tw`, `%tq` and `%th`. I'm not sure that there are corresponding formats available in R. So far they are imported as integers.

title: A dedicated package for labelled variables
description:
The labelled class is defined in `haven`. Therefore, `haven` is required to manipulate such variables with functions as `as_factor`. In future, we could think that other import packages could also use such class. Furthermore, it could be appropriate to develop some functions to manipulate labelled variable.

Some examples:

``` r
label(d$x) # to get the variable label
label(d$x) <- "variable label" # to modify the variable label
label(d$x, 2) # to get the value label of variable x for value 2
label(d$x, 2) <- "Yes" # to modify the value label of variable x for value 2
summary(d$x) # to present a frequency table of d$x with global percent and valid percent (taking into account declared missing values)
```

etc.

Therefore, would it be more appropriate to have a dedicated package?

title: write_dta not including format
description: Using R 3.2.1, haven 0.2, and Stata 14, `write_dta` does not create browsable data for Stata. All the data is present and usable in Stata, but the columns in a haven-exported file lack a format, so Stata does not display them in the browse window. Here's a minimal example: ``` library(dplyr) library(haven) library(foreign) set.seed(1234) example_data <- data_frame(var1 = rnorm(20, 0, 1), var2 = rnorm(20, 2, 5), var3 = runif(20, -10, 10), var4 = factor(sample(letters, 20))) write_dta(example_data, path="with_haven.dta") write.dta(example_data, file="with_foreign.dta") ``` With foreign, everything works well: With haven, there is no format (`%9.0g`) and all the columns are blank, but the data is still there (see top red box). If I add a format manually, the data displays just fine.

title: SPSS complains that columns from file made using write_sav are constant
description:
You closed issue #51 because I had not added a reproducible example and told me to re-open. I provided one, but it is not possible to re-open an issue as a user, so I just left it.

Anyway, the problem apparently still persists and is easy to reproduce:

Do

``` r
library(haven)
mtcars[1,1] = NA
write_sav(mtcars,"~/Downloads/mtcars.sav")
```

open mtcars.sav in SPSS

```
CORRELATIONS 
  /VARIABLES=mpg cyl 
  /PRINT=TWOTAIL NOSIG 
  /MISSING=PAIRWISE.

title: Importing only selected columns from SPSS files
description:
This is a feature request.

It would be great to be able to read (at least SPSS files) and import only selected columns. A bit like the functions in the `memisc` package. SPSS files are used to distribute data from surveys which contain a lot of variables (e.g. 10k) which are never used simultaneously. Loading entire data is usualy either impossible (not enough RAM) or takes a lot of time, and is usually needed only to create a subset.

In general, I was thinking whether it would be possible to work with SPSS files a bit like with database data sources in `dplyr`, but limited to `select` and perhaps `filter` operations... It would definitely be useful for a lot of people. At this moment `foreign::read.spss` can load only whole data files, and functions in `memisc` do not support data files produced with recent versions of SPSS.

title: Return values requre  a lot of cleanup
description:
I've been kicking the tires on haven, and am really happy to see a fast and modern package for importing data from other statistical packages. Thanks to Hadley and everyone else who contributed for all their hard work! It is very nice indeed to have a package that reliably imports Stata version > 12 data sets. 

I have encountered a number of difficulties using the package, which I have tried to illustrate and describe at https://gist.github.com/izahn/db16d52ed6b4289425bb. In one way or another I think these all involve the decision to store metadata as variable-level attributes rather than as data.frame level attributes as the foreign package does. 

Specifically:
1. Using `str` on data read with haven is not as useful because the attributes make the output very noisy, and because everything just says "atomic" rather than providing information about the variable type.
2. Cleaning up data imported with haven is not easy because it doesn't appear to try to work out what type each column should be. Rather it seems to store everything as a double along with the metadata, and leaves it to the user to sort out. This is somewhat ironic, since one purpose of metadata is to provide information to the computer so that it can represent the data appropriately.

I realize these are somewhat broad points, and I don't have a sense of how difficult it would be to address these issues. I don't know C, but I'm happy to help with R coding, testing, or anything else I can do to help make haven more user-friendly.

title: BUG: When one tries to access a non-existing variable label  the value labels are returned
description:
When haven reads SPSS/sav files it also reads in variable labels and value labels to construct a vector of the class labelled, where the variable label is stored in attributes(foo)$label and the variable labels are stored in attributes(foo)$labels.

This distinction breaks down if the labelled vector has only value labels but not variable label. In this case, haven will return the value labels when it is asked for the variable label with attributes(foo)$label or attr(foo,"label") and only correctly return NULL with attributes(foo)[["label"]].

Maybe there is something I don't know about how one should access entries in a list, but it seems wrong to me that 2 out of 3 attempts to access a variable attribute return incorrect results.

title: write_dta should use the smallest possible integral type
description:
Currently all `integer` and `logical` vectors are written as `READSTAT_TYPE_INT32` (Stata's `long`). Stata has two smaller integral types: `byte` and `int` (16 bits). The memory savings from using smaller types can be quite significant when working with large datasets.

write_dta should write all `logical` vectors as `byte` variables, and select the most efficient type for `integer` vectors (by calculating the max and min value).

title: write_sav() truncates long labels
description:
Below is a reproducible example of a situation where haven::write_sav exports an SPSS file that contains incorrect value labels. When one adds labels to a character variable (making it a labelled vector in R because you want it to have value labels in the exported SPSS file) and at least one of the actual values in that variable is >= 9 characters in length, then the labels are not correctly exported for that variable. Labels may be fine for other variables in the same file. Labels are correctly exported if all values for the variable in question have <= 8 characters. When I use SPSS to inspect the value labels in test_export.sav, I see a value that looks like  "12345678lz h□" where I should see "12345678E". Similarly, I see "1234ABCD{z h□" where I should see "1234ABCD". I've extended the code to show what is actually read back in via read_sav(). 

`````` R
# Write_sav() does not properly export value labels in the SPSS file for 
# labelled character variables when at least one value of that variable 
# contains 9 or more characters. 

# Create example data. v1 should export correctly because all values are 
# <= 8 characters, v2 will not because first value is 9 characters long.  
dat <- data.frame(v1 = c("12345678",  "ABCDEFGH", "1234ABCD"),
                  v2 = c("12345678E", "ABCDEFGH", "1234ABCD"),
                  l1 = c("Text1",  "Text2", "Text3"),
                  l2 = c("Text4",  "Text5", "Text6"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Create a named vector from a vector of values plus a vector of labels.
named <- function(x, labels) {names(x) <- labels; return(x)}

# Turn v1 & v2 into labelled variables so they'll have value labels 
# assigned in the exported SPSS file. Length & contents of the strings 
# in the label vectors seem not to matter. 
dat$v1 <- labelled(dat$v1, named(dat$v1, dat$l1))
dat$v2 <- labelled(dat$v2, named(dat$v2, dat$l2))
dat
str(dat)

# The SPSS file created below will have correct value labels only for v1. 
# You have to open the file in SPSS to see that. 
write_sav(dat, path = "test_export.sav")

# Read the file back in to show that what was stored in test_export.sav
# does not match properties of the data frame written out. 
dat2 <- read_sav(path = "test_export.sav")
str(dat2)

# Correct set of labels we tried to write out. 
attr(dat$v2, "labels")

# Incorrect set of labels recovered from the exported file. 
attr(dat2$v2, "labels") ``` 


``````

title: as_factor returning labels with both numerical code and value labels
description:
When working with labelled data, it's often very useful to have a feedback with both numerical code and value labels.

For example, I have a custom `lfactor` function (cf. https://github.com/larmarange/JLutils/blob/master/R/label_freq.R) with an option `add.codes` to return a factor with labels looking like:
- [1] Woman
- [2] Man

instead of
- Man
- Woman

In fact, seeing both numerical codes and value labels is useful when developing an analysis while for the final results we usually wants only the value labels.

PS: a more general question. It seems that several persons (@sjPlot for example) are starting to develop functions to deal with labelled variables. Do you have any plan to develop a dedicated package where such functions could be integrated?

title: additional argument for as_factor
description:

Currently `as_factor.labelled` apply `NA` to values who don't have a corresponding label. It would be great to have a option to keep these values (and in that case to crate a level whose label would be the original numeric code).

title: wish: encoding parameter for read_sas()
description:
sas7bdat files can report an incorrect encoding. In this case it would be helpful if one could overrule the stated encoding by a parameter like:

> read_sas('xy.sas7bdat', encoding = 'ISO-8859-15')

Old sas7bdat files do not store their encoding at all. ReadStat's readstat_sas.c defines SAS_DEFAULT_STRING_ENCODING to resolve to WINDOWS-1252 in these cases. It would be great if from R one could overrule this setting either by another parameter to read_sas() or (better I think) by an option "defaultSASencoding" or so.

An example dataset with Shift-JIS content but no encoding specified you find in [https://github.com/reikoch/testfiles/blob/master/tt.sas7bdat](url)

title: read_spss() imports value labels for multiple declared missings
description:
In SPSS, you can assign multiple missing values, e.g. "8" as "not applicable" or "9" for "real missing". `read_spss()` would set both 8 and 9 to `NA` in the imported data.frame, however, if a value label for "8" is set, it is also imported - thus, you have one more value label than values.

Example:

"Do you live in partnership?"

1 - yes
2 - no
8 - not applicable (was asked before if married) -> declared as "8" missing
9 - missing -> declared as "9" missing, but not labelled

Now read_spss() imports this as vector with two values (1/2) and NA's, but three value labels (yes/no/not applicable).

This is no serious bug, but I wonder if it would be possible to distinguish whether an SPSS-declared "missing value" is either a "real" missing or a "not applicable" declared missing. In SPSS you do this e.g. to get valid frequency counts for yes/no answers, but still having the information how much "real" missings you have...

title: `as_factor.labelled` should preserve the variable label
description:
When convert a `labelled` vector to a factor using `as_factor`, the variable name, stored in the attribute `label`, should be preserved. I'd be happy to contribute a pull request if you deem this a good idea.

Example:

```
# Create a labelled vector with both (variable) label and (value) labels
my_var <- sample(c(0, 1), 10, replace = TRUE)
class(my_var) <- "labelled"
attr(my_var, "label") <- "My Variable"
attr(my_var, "labels") <- c("Agree" = 1, "Disagree" = 0)


my_var # Has both variable label and value labels
as_factor(my_var) # No longer has the variable label
```

title: as_factor drops unused labels when levels = "default".
description:
As title states, `as_factor.labelled` drops unused labels when `levels = "default"` (or "both").

Example:

``` r
  s1 <- labelled(rep(1, 3), c("A" = 1, "B" = 2, "C" = 3))
  exp <- factor(rep("A", 3), levels = c("A", "B", "C"))
  str(as_factor(s1, levels = "default"))
  # Factor w/ 1 level "A": 1 1 1
```

Maybe this is intended, but I'd like to propose that the default should include all labels to safely (and easily) convert labelled variables to factors without information-loss. Users can instead explicitly call `droplevels()` after converting to produce the result above.

-Kristian

title: Accessing labelled tagged NAs
description:
I'm very impressed by the new `NA` mechanism of haven, especially the tagged NA is a brilliant feature. For some functions of my package, I need to know which labelled NA corresponds to which NA tag:

```
x <- c(1:3, tagged_na("a", "c", "z"), 3:1)
y <- labelled(x, c("First" = tagged_na("c"), "Refused" = tagged_na("a"), "Not home" = tagged_na("z")))
str(y)
```

> Class 'labelled'  atomic [1:9] 1 2 3 NA NA NA 3 2 1
>   ..- attr(_, "labels")= Named num [1:3] NA NA NA
>   .. ..- attr(_, "names")= chr [1:3] "First" "Refused" "Not home"

```
format_tagged_na(y)
```

> [1] "    1" "    2" "    3" "NA(a)" "NA(c)" "NA(z)" "    3" "    2" "    1"

title: A Stata-like `codebook` function that quickly summarises a variable
description:
`codebook` is a Stata function that gives a quick overview of a variable (its name, missingness, range, value, labels). (See image). Stata users frequently ask for this function when they switch to R.

![stata_codebook](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4418241/15945884/60c1f2cc-2e62-11e6-8460-6b4e0fc8f2a1.png)

Is this something `haven` wants to implement with regards to its `labelled` class?
- Argument for: With `codebook`, `haven` would attract even more Stata users & teams.
- Argument against: `labelled` is a temporary class to be converted into `factor`.

Happy to contribute PR if you think it's a good idea.

title: Is it possible to have a `add_val_labels()` function for pipeline?
description:
Right now if one wants to add value labels for a variable, it would be something like the following:

``` R
df = tibble::data_frame(s1 = c("M", "M", "F"), s2 = c(1, 1, 2))
df$s1 = haven::labelled(df$s1, c(Male = "M", Female = "F"))
df$s2 = haven::labelled(df$s2, c(Male = 1, Female = 2))
```

I was wondering if there can be a function `add_val_lables()` so that one can do

``` R
df %>%
    add_val_labels(s1, c(Male = "M", Female = "F")) %>%
    add_val_labels(s2, c(Male = 1, Female = 2)) 
```

Or

``` R
df %>%
    add_val_labels(s1, s1 == "M" ~ "Male", s1 == "F" ~ "Female") %>%
    add_val_labels(s2, s2 == 1 ~ "Male", s2 == 2 ~ "Female") 
```

title: write_dta problem: with factor variables, NA written as large integer, not recognized as Stata missings
description:
write_dta() applied to a tbl_df containing a factor variable with NA values generates a Stata .dta file in which NA values are written as the large integer "2147483621".  Stata does recognize this integer as a missing value.

Requires post-processing in Stata (.do file below) to recode the large integer to missing. Significant compression is also possible via  'compress'.

```
foreach var of varlist _all {
   replace `var'= .  if `var' == 2147483621
}
compress
```

Reproducible example below:

```
test <- structure(list(InjuryMech = structure(c(12L, NA, 7L), .Label = c("Occupant in motor vehicle collision (MVC)",  "Pedestrian struck by moving vehicle", "Bike rider struck by automobile", 
"Bike collision or fall from bike while riding", "Other wheeled transport crash", 
"Fall to ground from standing/walking/running", "Walked or ran into stationary object", 
"Fall from an elevation", "Fall down stairs", "Sports", "Assault", 
"Object struck head - accidental", "Other mechanism"), class = "factor"), 
    High_impact_InjSev = structure(c(2L, NA, 1L), .Label = c("Low", 
    "Moderate", "High"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("InjuryMech", 
"High_impact_InjSev"), class = c("tbl_df", "data.frame"), row.names = c(NA, 
-3L))

title: Support multiple missing values
description:
SAS and Stata support "tagged" missing values: `.A`, `.B`, ..., `.Z`, and for SAS `._`. SPSS supports per-column user defined missing values: either up to 3 distinct values, or a range plus 1 distinct value. Haven needs to capture these special missing values in a way that preserves regular R missing values semantics, while enabling them to be labelled.

Replaces #33 & #118

title: Binary SAS file compression unsupported
description: See https://github.com/WizardMac/ReadStat/issues/21

title: write_sav and strings with > 256 characters?
description:
Not sure if this is a bug or a feature, but `write_sav` seems to have a max string length of 256 character vectors and truncates the rest without warning. A quick example that produces a error in the latest version (`0.2.0.9000`):

```
test_that("can roundtrip long strings", {
  x <- paste0(rep(letters, 10), collapse = "")
  expect_equal(roundtrip_var(x), x)
})
```

Since both SPSS and R can store strings that are longer than 256 characters, is this some limitation in the underlying C++ code or a design choice?

title: as_factor has odd behaviour when applied to zeros
description:
I have some data where many data values are zero as a meaningful category and this is labelled. There seems to be some kind of unexpected behaviour when  apply as_factor to a labelled vector with zero values. This behaviour seems to come and go, so I'm not sure if this example will definitely reproduce. 

```
library(haven)
x <- labelled(c(0, 1, 1,0 ), c(Bad = 0, Good = 1))
```

The vector appears to have been created correctly here:

<Labelled>
[1] 0 1 1 0
Labels:
 Bad Good 
   0    1 
However conversion to factor gives just about the worst possible outcome:

```
   as_factor(x)
```

[1] Good NA NA Good
Levels: Bad Good

Would it be appropriate to add the command `options(width = 80)` in that test? (https://github.com/hadley/haven/blob/master/tests/testthat/test-tagged_na.R#L57)

title: Is it possible for `haven` to import dataset attributes from Stata?
description:
# Background

Stata has various dataset attributes, such as 
- dataset label, 
- last saved date, 
- short notes that allow dataset maintainer to include other metadata: data source, sample, maintainer email, etc.

Take the dataset `nlsw88` for example. Once loaded, it prints out a short dataset label:

![webuse](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11262574/16166753/b62c7dc0-34b3-11e6-9656-4c9ba32f5af0.png)

The next thing a typical Stata user would do is probably use the `describe` command to get a basic idea about the dataset. As shown in the following screenshot, the `d` command print out a header that shows data label, last saved date, and indicates that there're more notes about this dataset.

![describe](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11262574/16166955/85d915b4-34b5-11e6-8889-fe875137ece2.png)

The `notes` command can then prints out these notes:

![notes](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11262574/16166957/88b08542-34b5-11e6-9915-490742987071.png)

The `codebook, header` command shows similar dataset attributes:

![cb-header](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11262574/16166967/9953c116-34b5-11e6-99aa-be9a7d61d081.png)
# Feature Request

Right now `haven` is not preserving these dataset level attributes. I was wondering if it's possible to keep them, as it's done in the `foreign` package:

``` R
foreign::read.dta("http://www.stata-press.com/data/r12/nlsw88.dta") %>% str()
#> 'data.frame': 2246 obs. of  17 variables:
#> ...
#> - attr(*, "datalabel")= chr "NLSW, 1988 extract"
#> - attr(*, "time.stamp")= chr "1 May 2011 22:52"
#> - attr(*, "formats")= chr  "%8.0g" "%8.0g" "%8.0g" "%8.0g" ...
#> - attr(*, "types")= int  252 251 251 251 251 251 251 251 251 251 ...
#> - attr(*, "val.labels")= chr  "" "" "racelbl" "marlbl" ...
#> - attr(*, "var.labels")= chr  "NLS id" "age in current year" "race" "married" ...
#> - attr(*, "expansion.fields")=List of 7
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note1" "1988 data, extracted from National Longitudinal of Young Woman"
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note2" "who were ages 14-24 in 1968 (NLSW)."
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note3" "This dataset is the result of extraction and processing by various"
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note4" "people at various times."
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note5" "For more information on the NLS, see"
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note0" "6"
#> ..$ : chr  "_dta" "note6" "http://www.bls.gov/nls/"
#> - attr(*, "version")= int 12
```

`foreign` is not doing quite correctly for keeping "format", "types", "val.labels", and "var.labels" as these attributes belong to corresponding variables, but I believe it'd be worthwhile to keep others at the dataset level.

Moreover, it might also be useful for `tibble` to print out some of these attributes, and indicate that there're more detailed notes.

Probably related: [hadley/tibble#90](https://github.com/hadley/tibble/issues/90)

title: `write_sav` issues with labelled class vectors
description:
I have found some issues when saving labelled data to SPSS. I used the latest dev-build from 25th June. First, here is the reproducible example for the issues:

```
library(haven)
x <- labelled(c(1:3, tagged_na("a", "c", "z"), 4:1),
              c("Agreement" = 1, "äquivalent" = 2, "Disagreement" = 4, "First" = tagged_na("c"),
                "Refused" = tagged_na("a"), "Not home" = tagged_na("z")))

attr(x, "label") <- "Äquivalenzeinkommen"
x
# test.sav
haven::write_sav(data.frame(test = x), "test.sav")
# test2.sav
haven::write_sav(data.frame(test = haven::as_factor(x)), "test2.sav")
```

Now to what I have found:
- Using the `data.frame` method on a labelled vector produces a column name with dots at the end. Dots are no legal characters at the end of variable names in SPSS. Trying to run any command with this variable leads to an error in SPSS.

```
> data.frame(x)
   x..i..
1       1
2       2
3       3
4      NA
```

![spss_2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4901179/16392000/03b9cca2-3caa-11e6-80c4-598decd00be9.png)
- It seems that the "tags" of tagged NA values are saved, but recognized as invalid value labels. See screenshot and also the screenshot above:

![spss_1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4901179/16391961/d43502da-3ca9-11e6-9a6a-cc3e6cf98c70.png)
- After changing the variable name, the value labels are not correctly assigned. See screenshot above, where 1 is agreement, 2 is äquivalenz and 4 is disagreement. Running the frequency command in SPSS gives following:

![spss_4](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4901179/16392104/7392d636-3caa-11e6-8fc7-bbe873039111.png)
- After editing some of the value labels, assignment still is not correct:

![spss_5](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4901179/16392117/855cab9e-3caa-11e6-9ef1-97c1ad5741ee.png)

To summarise, `labelled` vectors are not properly saved to SPSS. **However**, _factors_ are. The second SPSS file, where I used `haven::as_factor(x))`, seems to work, except that `as_factor` does not convert values to NA (thus, they are counted as regular values).
- Correct value labels

![spss_try2_2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4901179/16392167/d2f9e16e-3caa-11e6-81d3-2d1b3a096b2b.png)
- Correct frequencies

![spss_try2_1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4901179/16392181/db125458-3caa-11e6-9e5f-b9de21dec84d.png)
1. I would suggest to convert any labelled vector to factor with `as_factor` before writing the data.
2. Furthermore, it would be nice to include an option, where (tagged/labelled) NA values can be converted to NA. You have to be sure to convert them to regular NA (i.e. removing the "tag" from the NA value), else you have broken value labels (see 1st/2nd screenshot at top)

[Test1 and 2.zip](https://github.com/hadley/haven/files/335621/Test1.and.2.zip)

title: read_sas : wrong labels when importing formats
description:
Hello,

When importing SAS dataset with formatted variables, labels and values seem to match correctly only if possible values are given in the good (alphabetical?) order in the _proc format._

Here is a test data generated in SAS :

```
proc format lib=mylib.test_formats ;
 /* both A and B formats are identical, only order of possible values is different*/
 value $A
   "1" = "Male"
   "2" = "Female" ;
 value $B
   "2" = "Female"
   "1" = "Male" ;
run ;

data mylib.test_data ;
   input ID $ SEXA $ SEXB $ ;
   format SEXA $A. SEXB $B. ;
   datalines ;
     ID1 1 1
     ID2 2 2
     ID3 1 1
   ;
run ;
```

The problem arises when importing in R :

```
test_data <- read_sas(
  b7dat = "test_data.sas7bdat", 
  b7cat = "test_formats.sas7bcat")

attr(test_data$SEXA, "labels")
attr(test_data$SEXB, "labels")

test_data$fSEXA <- as_factor(test_data$SEXA)
test_data$fSEXB <- as_factor(test_data$SEXB)

test_data
```

The resulting data.frame is wrong for factor fSEXB :

```
   ID SEXA SEXB  fSEXA  fSEXB
1 ID1    1    1   Male Female
2 ID2    2    2 Female   Male
3 ID3    1    1   Male Female
```

title: as_factor: incorrect labelling for numeric 'labelled' vectors with non-positive values
description:
I ran into an issue with missing values appearing in factors when converting `labelled` variables (imported from an SPSS `.sav` file) into `factors` using `as_factor`. It seems conversion from a `labelled` vector to a `factor` using `as_factor` fails when the original `labelled` vector has labels assigned to non-positive values. This seems to be caused by the `match(x, labs)` used in creating the `factor` in `haven:::as_factor.labelled` for non-character vectors.

Here's a sample snippet:

```
> x <- labelled(c(-1, 0, 1), c(A = -1, B = 0, C  = 1))
> x
-1 0 1 
[1] -1  0  1
attr(,"labels")
 A  B  C 
-1  0  1 
> as_factor(x)
[1] C    <NA> <NA>
Levels: A B C
```

(Tested with R version 3.3.1.)

title: `droplevels()` removes "label" attribute from a labelled vector
description:
The following code emulates a variable I might get from using `read_sav()`, although here I am adding the `label` attribute afterward.

``` R
library(dplyr)
likert <- labelled(sample(4, 100, replace = TRUE),
                   c("Strongly Agree" = 1,
                     "Agree" = 2,
                     "Neutral" = 3,
                     "Disagree" = 4,
                     "Strongly Disagree" = 5))
attr(likert, "label") <- "Likert Scale"
likert %>% str()
# Class 'labelled'  atomic [1:100] 4 3 4 3 1 3 4 3 4 3 ...
# ..- attr(*, "labels")= Named num [1:5] 1 2 3 4 5
# .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:5] "Strongly Agree" "Agree" "Neutral" "Disagree" ...
# ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "Likert Scale"
```

Is there a way to preserve the variable label if I want to drop unused levels?

``` R
likert %>% as_factor() %>% str()
# Factor w/ 5 levels "Strongly Agree",..: 4 3 4 3 1 3 4 3 4 3 ...
# - attr(*, "label")= chr "Likert Scale"
likert %>% as_factor() %>% droplevels() %>% str()
# Factor w/ 4 levels "Strongly Agree",..: 4 3 4 3 1 3 4 3 4 3 ...
```

title: read_sas: "b7dat" and "b7cat" are inaccurate parameter names

- `data_file`/`catalog_file`

title: Support stata value labels longer than 32 characters
description:
Stata allows value labels longer than 32 characters, but haven write_dta() does not permit them.

To create a demonstration data set, in Stata do:  (Update: added a .zip of this file, below.)

    use http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/stata/modules/autolab.dta, clear
    label define foreignlabels 0 "Hey everybody I am a domestic car" 1 "Hey everybody I am a foreign car"
    label values foreign foreignlabels
    save "autolab.dta"

Then in R we observe:

    > nchar("Hey everybody I am a domestic car")
    [1] 33

and

    > k <- read_dta('autolab.dta')   # adjust path as needed
    > write_dta(k, 'test-out.dta')
    Error: Stata only supports value labels up to 32 characters in length. 
    Problems: `foreign`

The length limit of the label name definition (in this case 'foreignlabels') is in fact 32, but the current limit to the value labels themselves is 32,000, according to http://www.stata.com/help.cgi?limits.

title: SPSS fails to read value labels for ordered factors
description:
SPSS is unable to read value labels for ordered factors -- whereas unordered factors are fine.

A minimal example:

```{r}
x <- c("a", "b", "c")

df <- data.frame(
  v1 = factor(x),
  v2 = factor(x, ordered = TRUE)
)

library(haven)
write_sav(df, "df.sav")
```

Here is a screenshot of the SPSS **Data View** tab after I open the file in SPSS:

![data_view](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/18112792/25324684/b20d3794-28f9-11e7-81d5-fcd82f1ca7c6.png)

`v1` and `v2` should look identical - however for `v2` the numeric values rather than the factor labels are displayed.

On the SPSS **Variable View** tab, for the unordered factor `v1`, SPSS correctly displays the measure type as `Nominal` and the value labels are listed correctly in the `Values` column. title: new function suggestion: get_var_labels
description:

Currently I use the following function from this [thread](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10181730/information-from-label-attribute-in-r-to-variable-labels-in-spss):

```
get_var_labels = function(data) {
  a = do.call(Hmisc::llist, data)
  tempout = vector("list", length(a))

  for (i in 1:length(a)) {
    tempout[[i]] = Hmisc::label(a[[i]])
  }
  b = unlist(tempout)
  structure(c(b), .Names = names(data))
}
```
It would be handy if this function formed part of the `haven` package without having to be dependent on `Hmisc`

title: read_spss: When a missing value is not defined as a value label
description:
Hi,

Consider a .sav file with several numeric variables where -77 is defined as a missing value, but not as a value label. You would get the following result when trying to index one of them:

```
ds <- read_spss(sav.file, user_na=TRUE)
ds[1]
Error: `x` and `labels` must be same type
```

I'm sure there are plenty of ways to fix it, but I'm looking for a solution that doesn't require operations outside of R, and is faster than a loop. Running user_na=FALSE will avoid the issue, but I need the actual values, NA won't do. The only solution i've found is:

```
ds <- read_spss(sav.file, user_na=TRUE)
val_label(ds[[1]], -77) <- "temp"
na_values(ds[[1]]) <- NULL 
val_label(ds[[1]], -77) <- NULL
```

It's not great, and I don't think I can avoid a for-loop since the solution won't work without double brackets. Can anyone suggest a fast way to perform the above operation on multiple columns in a large dataset?

This may be kind of a fringe issue. The .sav files have been put together by a supplier's computer system. It would be great if there was an option to completely ignore SPSS missing values altogether when performing an import, as opposed to importing them as attributes that can potentially mess things up when dealing with sub-par datasets.

Thanks in advance!

This is on a cluster account (no root privileges).  Non-R libraries that I require, such as `libiconv` are built and installed into a local path, and that path is included in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.  I have verified that `Sys.getenv("LD_LIBRARY_PATH")` includes the path to **libiconv.so**.

## Expected behavior
R should use `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable to resolve linked libraries, in this case `libiconv`.

title: write_sav() sometimes writes invalid SPSS files for UTF-8 encoded strings (on Windows)
description:
When a tibble contains an UTF-8 encoded string, `write_sav()` *sometimes* generates invalid SPSS files (on Windows, and under a latin1 locale). I have finally managed to reduce the problem a *relatively* simple, and reproducible, example:

```r
library(haven)
d1 <- tibble::tibble(test="Spørsmålene under handler om hvordan du oppfatter helsen din. Disse opplysningene vil hjelpe oss til å forstå hvordan du føler deg og hvor godt du er i stand til å utføre dine vanlige aktiviteter. Hvert spørsmål skal besvares ved å sette et krys")
d2 <- d1
d2$test <- paste0(d2$test, "s")

d1$test <- iconv(d1$test, to="utf8")
d2$test <- iconv(d2$test, to="utf8")
write_sav(d1, "h:/utf-d1.sav")
write_sav(d2, "h:/utf-d2.sav")
```

When I open the `utf-d1.sav` file in SPSS, everything is fine. When I try to open the `utf-d2.sav` file in SPSS (version 24), I get following error message (and the file is not opened, but locked for additional saving):

```
GET
  FILE='H:\utf-d2.sav'.

>Error.  Command name: GET FILE
>Invalid SPSS Statistics data file: H:\utf-d2.sav (DATA1204)
>Execution of this command stops.

>Error # 1405 in column 8.  Text: H:\utf-d2.sav
>Error when attempting to get a data file.
```

# Additional notes

R encodes strings as `latin1` by default on Windows. That’s why I have reencoded them to UTF-8 (I often have UTF-8-encoded tibbles, e.g. from `read_excel()`). Also note that the only difference between `d1` and `d2` is that the `test` variable has an extra `s` character, which seems to make all the difference. :/

It may of course be possible that *both* files are actually invalid, but that SPSS manages to recover for the first file but not from the second.

Reading the files using `read_sav()` seems to work fine.

Saving the tibbles *without* reencoding the strings to UTF-8 first leads to #258.

title: SPSS system missings read as NaN
description:
After installing the v1.0.0 update I noticed a bunch of `NaN`s in datasets I have been importing to R from SPSS using `read_sav()`.

It appears that the `.` or system missing values in my `.sav` files are now being read into R as `NaN` rather than `NA`.

Here is a [dataset](https://github.com/tidyverse/haven/files/503434/data.zip) with just one variable to illustrate the issue.

This variable has 12 missing values in the `.sav` file, and when imported with haven v0.2.0 we see 12 `NA`s in R.  Then when imported with haven v1.0.0 we see 12 `NaN`s in R.

Here is code to reproduce the issue with that dataset:

```
remove.packages("haven")

# with v0.2.0 the 12 missing values are read in as NA
devtools::install_version("haven", version = "0.2.0", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
data <- haven::read_sav("data.sav")
table(data$var1, useNA = "always")

remove.packages("haven")

# with v1.0.0 the 12 missing values are read in as NaN
install.packages("haven") # v1.0.0
data <- haven::read_sav("data.sav")
table(data$var1, useNA = "always")
```

title: support labelled logical vectors [feature request]
description:
I'd like to be able to create a labelled logical vector like this:

```R
library(haven)
logi_var = labelled(rep(TRUE, 5), c("some label" = TRUE, "some other label" = FALSE))
```

Right now this is not supported and gives the error message:
```R
`x` must be a numeric or a character vector`
```

Of course one can always set the corresponding attributes "by hand" using:
```R
logi_var <- rep(T, 5)
attr(x = logi_var, which = "class") <- "labelled"
attr(x = logi_var, which = "labels") <- c("some label" = TRUE, "some other label" = FALSE)
```
Naive as I am  [I tried this in the past (unknowingly about the interplay between `dplyr` and `haven`)](https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/3108).

Now because the `labelled()` constructor is called when `select()`ing on dataframes, I was only confronted with the error message – which of course didn't make any sense to me at that time:
```R
library(dplyr)
df <- data_frame(logi_var)
df %>% select(logi_var)
#> Error: `x` must be a numeric or a character vector
```

Therefore my question: Is there any specific reason to not support labelled logical vectors?

And if not, my request: Please add support for it! :slightly_smiling_face:
